A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SDTagNet work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable, and retained content can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original SDTagNet evaluations on Argoverse 2 and nuScenes, together with component ablations, augmentation experiments, and qualitative analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds SDTagNet evaluations under another label and split configuration in Table 2, plus computational measurements in Table 10.

M1.justification: The contrastively pretrained BERT tag encoder, point-level queries, orthogonal random feature identifiers, and decoder cross-attention remain unchanged. Section 3.3 explains the existing point, polyline, and relation representations more explicitly without introducing a different procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use Argoverse 2, nuScenes, and OpenStreetMap. v2 additionally evaluates a three-class Argoverse 2 task covering dividers, boundaries, and pedestrian crossings in Table 2, alongside the retained five-class evaluation. This modestly broadens task coverage without adding a dataset or driving domain.

E2.justification: New Table 2 substantially broadens the comparisons by including HIMap, MapUnveiler, StreamMapNet, and MapTracker, which were not evaluated against SDTagNet in v1. The existing MapTRv2, PMapNet, and SMERF comparisons remain. The new table incorporates published comparator scores, explicitly sourcing StreamMapNet values from MapTracker.

E3.justification: Table 2 adds a distinct evaluation regime using the original Argoverse 2 split and the StreamMapNet geographic split, with a 100 m x 50 m far-range area. This differs from the retained experiments using the Lilja geographic split and 120 m x 60 m far-range area. The table reports differing comparator training budgets, and Appendix A.6 additionally introduces H100-based speed and memory profiling. Existing protocols are retained.

E4.justification: Appendix A.6 adds an analysis of computational overhead relative to MapTRv2, PMapNet, and SMERF. The existing component, fine-tuning, attention, augmentation, and geographic-overlap analyses remain unchanged. The architectural ablation in Table 3 is moved into the main text rather than newly conducted.

E5.justification: New Table 10 explicitly reports averaging the efficiency measurements over 10 samples, adding limited measurement-aggregation information absent from v1. This does not establish ten independent training runs; neither version supplies seed variability, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: All eight original tables retain their numerical results after matching renumbered tables. New Table 2 adds substantial accuracy evidence: SDTagNet reports near/far mAP of 78.0/78.3 on the original split and 67.8/70.9 on the StreamMapNet geographic split. These are additional results under different settings, not improvements over v1's scores. Table 10 also adds computational results, including 50.54 million parameters, 14.5 FPS, and 3686 MB VRAM for SDTagNet.

T1.justification: The QR-based construction of orthogonal random features and the contrastive-learning reasoning are retained. The expanded representation description restates existing mathematics and Figure 4; no new formal assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and conclusion retain the same novelty claims, proposed components, and headline far-range improvements. The added comparisons extend supporting evidence without redefining these core contributions.

C2.justification: Appendix A.6 newly interprets the measured runtime and memory overhead as supporting real-time deployment. Section 4.3 also emphasizes far-range competitiveness against temporal methods despite SDTagNet's single-shot operation. Existing explanations concerning geographic overfitting, map discrepancies, and incorrect one-way direction predictions remain substantively unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix A.6 and Table 10 add inference-profiling hardware and measurement details, while the acknowledgements identify the HoreKa computing facility. Existing pretraining settings, baseline implementation details, training hardware and budgets, and code/data access statements remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds the MapUnveiler reference and explicitly positions SDTagNet against recent methods without SD-map priors in Section 4.3. The related-work discussion otherwise remains substantially unchanged; several other bibliography edits update publication metadata for already cited works.

P1.justification: v2 clarifies the ORF representation explanation, repairs the unresolved cross-reference in Section 3.3, and moves architectural-ablation discussion from Appendix A.1 into Section 4.3. It also adds acknowledgements and an efficiency subsection, with limited wording edits elsewhere rather than extensive rewriting.

P2.justification: v2 adds comparison Table 2 and efficiency Table 10, relocates Table 3 into the main text, and rearranges other tables and surrounding text. Figure 7 now shares a page with its discussion and the efficiency table. The original figures retain their visual content and design.

improvement.justification: The added contemporary-method comparison and computational measurements improve the paper's empirical context and provide concrete support for previously asserted real-time feasibility. Clearer encoding explanations and more accessible ablations also help readers assess the method. The improvement is limited: comparison protocols and training budgets differ, efficiency evidence covers only 10 H100 samples, and the original method, accuracy results, and substantive limitations remain unchanged.
